To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) HRR is able to learn a structured representation of language, which is consistent with the classic division between syntax (structure) and semantics (meaning); 2) HRR is also able to learn the syntactic and semantic role of words and chunks in a sentence, which is consistent and compatible with classic linguistic theories of syntax and semantics.
HRR can be used to inject linguistic structure into neural language models, and that these models can learn to discover a crude linguistic distinction between syntax and semantics.

(1) we can decompose the representations of our neural language models into a syntactic and semantic component, (2) the syntactic component can be used to detect syntactic roles, and (3) the semantic component can be used as a semantic representation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two aspects of linguistic representation. (a) How to represent words and chunks in a way that is more structured and informative.
the following question: can a neural language model learn to decompose linguistic representations in a way that is informed by the HRR framework?
the question of how we can use HRR to build structured compositional representations in neural models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our model, with the HRR representation, can discover linguistic structures and linguistic role, but the quality and accuracy of the discovered structure and linguistic role are far away from the state-of-the-art models.
HRR is a useful tool in the quest of decomposing linguistic representations in neural networks.
our model can be seen as a first step towards decomposed linguistic representation, but it is not there yet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to learn structured representations from scratch and without any prior knowledge.
we propose to decompose the linguistic representation with a structured compositional approach, which is able to discover crude syntactic and semantic information.
we are able to learn a decomposed and interpretable representation from raw text.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by using a structured representation, we can gain a better understanding of the linguistic structure in our models.
we can decompose the linguistic representation into two distinct components, and that this is done without any supervision.
HRR can be a useful framework to build decomposed representations for neural NLP.
